one_sentence: God is proven when the deepest law of the fallen system encounters someone it cannot lawfully bind.
executive_summary: This document argues that God is proven not by a mere violation of a universal rule, but by a rightful exception—an exception that fulfills justice rather than breaking it. The key structural claim is that death, as the final law of fallen creation, holds jurisdiction only over what is sinful or corruptible; when Christ enters death without sin, death has no rightful claim and must release Him. This reframes resurrection as a structural verdict, not just a supernatural event, and establishes moral authority over the final law. The conclusion is that a true proof of God emerges when the deepest rule of the system testifies against itself by being unable to bind the one person who is its rightful superior.
short_summary: This document is a philosophical-theological argument for proving God through a rightful exception to the deepest rule of the fallen system. The core structural claim is that God is proven when the final law (death) encounters someone it cannot lawfully bind, not when a rule is arbitrarily broken. The key evidence is that Christ entered death sinlessly, so death had no jurisdiction and was forced to release Him, making resurrection a structural verdict. This matters because it grounds proof of God in moral authority and justice rather than mere power or anomaly.
